# Fix: java.nio.file.InvalidPathException - Routing Service NUL Character Error
## Problem Summary The routing service production module was throwing: ``` java.nio.file.InvalidPathException: Nul character not allowed: assg/service/OrToolsVrpService.classÝ ```
## Root Cause Analysis The error was caused by the `maven-dependency-plugin` with `unpack-dependencies` goal in `/tfms-starter/pom.xml`. This plugin was:
1. **Unpacking all module dependencies** (routing-service, auth-service, planner-service, etc.) into `${project.build.directory}/classes` 2. **Creating file path encoding issues** - When unpacking and repacking class files, byte encoding could become corrupted 3. **Introducing NUL characters** - The unpacking process was creating malformed paths with embedded NUL characters that couldn't be resolved during Spring Boot fat JAR creation 4. **Conflicting with Spring Boot packaging** - Spring Boot's fat JAR mechanism expects dependencies to remain as intact JAR files, not unpacked classes
## The Issue The corrupted character sequence "Ý" at the end of the path (`OrToolsVrpService.classÝ`) indicates binary corruption during the unpack/repack process. When the Spring Boot application tried to scan and load classes from the unpacked directory, it encountered invalid path encoding.
## Solution Applied **Removed the problematic `maven-dependency-plugin` configuration** from `/tfms-starter/pom.xml`:
### What Was Removed: ```xml <!-- REMOVED THIS: --> <plugin> <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId> <artifactId>maven-dependency-plugin</artifactId> <executions> <execution> <id>unpack-all-modules</id> <phase>prepare-package</phase> <goals> <goal>unpack-dependencies</goal> </goals> <configuration> <includeGroupIds>com.saxion.proj</includeGroupIds> <excludeArtifactIds>tfms-starter</excludeArtifactIds> <outputDirectory>${project.build.directory}/classes</outputDirectory> <excludes>META-INF/**,**/*Application.class</excludes> </configuration> </execution> </executions> </plugin> ```
### Why This Works: - **Spring Boot's Fat JAR mechanism** automatically handles all classpath dependencies - **Dependencies remain intact** as JAR files in the `BOOT-INF/lib/` directory of the fat JAR - **No file path corruption** occurs because classes are loaded from preserved JAR files, not unpacked directories - **Proper class loading** through Spring Boot's custom ClassLoader which handles multi-level JAR nesting correctly
## Verification ✅ Build completed successfully with all modules: - TFMS Commons - TFMS Auth Service - TFMS Routing Service - TFMS Planner Service - TFMS Starter Application
## Files Modified - `/home/prithvish/Documents/GitHub/02/tfms-starter/pom.xml` - Removed `maven-dependency-plugin` unpacking configuration - Removed corresponding m2e lifecycle mapping configuration
## Testing Recommendation After applying this fix: 1. Run `mvn clean install` to verify build succeeds 2. Run the application and verify routing service loads without errors 3. Monitor logs for any "InvalidPathException" or classpath-related errors
## Alternative Approaches If modular monolith requirements necessitate unpacking in the future: 1. Use Spring Boot 3.x's built-in modular support 2. Use a proper module system (JPMS - Java Platform Module System) 3. Keep modules as separate microservices with proper service discovery
